quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries press release: MHIET Establishes Hydrogen Co-Firing Specifications for the (08-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Group company Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Engine & Turbocharger (MHIET) established hydrogen co-firing specifications for its KU Series gas engines for power generation (output 3.65-5.75 MW, used in cogeneration systems) and has begun proposal activities; new installations can start on natural gas and later convert, existing KU Series gas engines can be retrofitted with minimal modifications, and the KU Diesel Engine (KU30A) can be converted via gas engine conversion. MHIET earlier confirmed stable combustion at rated output with up to 50 vol% hydrogen on a single-cylinder test engine for a 5.75MW gas engine. Company: gas engines are used as on-site power generation and in recent years to support grid stability; 'with electricity demand increasing globally, the need for gas engines is rising'; MHIET plans to expand hydrogen-capable models across its gas engine lineup.
quarterly_data.figure: 3.65-5.75 MW output; up to 50 vol% hydrogen co-firing (test engine)
